answer:
Evidence from support audits, customer testimony, and internal documentation supports the claim that scanned PDFs can weaken citation quality:

- **Support ticket data**: In May 2026, ingestion/OCR issues accounted for 112 of 412 tickets (about 27%), with roughly 40–50% of enterprise files being scanned PDFs without an embedded text layer. When TutorChat retrieves from these files, it either returns answers with no source citations because it cannot find text offsets, or the citation points to the entire document (e.g., page 1 of a 250-page PDF) rather than a specific section [NL-021#NL-021-S02].
- **Post-fix audit**: After the April fix, remaining citation tickets in May and June were "almost entirely linked to scanned, image-only PDFs," where TutorChat struggles to establish citation anchors and often links back to the start of the file instead of the specific page [NL-011#NL-011-S05].
- **Customer example**: At BrightPath, about 60% of clinical documentation consists of scanned, image-only PDFs. For a code blue response checklist query, the system answered correctly, but the citation pointed to page 1 of a 150-page document instead of page 87, forcing manual scrolling and breaking workflow [NL-018#NL-018-S04].
- **Root-cause documentation**: Scanned PDFs require OCR; without OCR, they cannot be searched and citations cannot be generated. OCR is heuristic, and blurry, low-resolution, handwritten, or complex-layout scans can cause "Broken Citations" where TutorChat cannot link to the exact paragraph [NL-006#NL-006-S03].
- **Cited root cause for missing citations**: A low-resolution scanned PDF is listed as a common cause for "No citation available" or broken link icons, because the layout parser cannot determine the exact page or section ID [NL-006#NL-006-S04].
- **Product guidance**: Low-quality scanned PDFs may prevent page-specific citations due to OCR limitations, and users are advised to re-save documents in a digital, text-searchable format [NL-028#NL-028-S03].
- **Planned warning/dashboard evidence**: Upload warnings describe scanned/image-only files as risking "poor citation quality," and the admin dashboard example flags `clinical_protocol_scan_v3.pdf` as a scanned PDF with only 45% citation confidence, versus 100% for successfully indexed documents [NL-021#NL-021-S05].
